title: Pain relief at home after surgery
also: how to relieve pain after discharge
what: At home, pain after surgery is relieved with pills on your doctor's schedule. A person whose pain is well controlled gets up and recovers faster.
why: After discharge, while a wound or joint heals.
duration: usually a few days or weeks, the pain gradually gets less
tell_doctor: Which painkillers have helped you before or did not suit you
If you drive or work with machinery

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: Before discharge ask for it to be written down: what to take, how much, at what time and for how long.

prepare.title: Pharmacy
prepare.text: Buy the painkillers in advance, so you are not left without them at night.

prepare.title: Other help
prepare.text: Ordinary ways help too: cold, a raised leg or arm, a comfortable position.

bring: The discharge summary with the pain relief schedule
steps: Take the painkiller by the clock, not only when the pain is already strong
Write down the time you took it, so you do not get confused
Do not go over the dose or combine similar medicines yourself
Apply cold through a cloth, if your doctor allows it
Move a little - this also reduces pain
When the pain eases, the dose is lowered on your doctor's advice
feel: The pain is usually stronger in the first days, then gets weaker
Some painkillers cause drowsiness or constipation
after: If the pain does not go away or grows, tell your surgeon
Do not drive if the medicine makes you drowsy
For constipation, drink more and move, and ask your doctor about a remedy
red_flags: The pain suddenly gets much worse or is different
Fever above 38, or the wound is red, hot or has pus
Black stools or vomiting blood - call your local emergency number
Severe drowsiness or slow breathing - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Can I wash down a painkiller with alcohol?
faq.a: No. Alcohol with painkillers is dangerous for the liver, stomach and breathing.

faq.q: What if the pain does not go away with pills?
faq.a: Do not raise the dose yourself. Call your surgeon or the clinic.

reminders.text: Time for your painkiller by the schedule. Mark the dose so you do not get confused.
